title: Hours of Operation
body: Little Acorns Learning Center is open Monday through Friday, 6:30 AM to 6:00 PM. Drop-off is welcome any time after 6:30 AM; we ask that children arrive by 9:30 AM so they can join the morning learning block. All children must be picked up by 6:00 PM.

title: Late Pickup Policy
body: There is a grace period until 6:05 PM. After 6:05 PM, a late fee of $1.00 per minute per child is added to the family's account and is due with the next weekly payment. After three late pickups in one calendar month, Director Maria Delgado will schedule a conversation with the family. If you are running late, please call (614) 555-0138 so we can reassure your child.

title: Holidays and Closures
body: The center is closed on New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, July 4th, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day and the day after Thanksgiving, and from December 24 through January 1. We also close for two staff in-service training days each year (typically one in February and one in August); dates are announced at least 60 days ahead. Tuition is not reduced for holiday closures.

title: Weather and Emergency Closures
body: We stay open in normal winter weather. We close or delay opening only if the county declares a Level 3 snow emergency or for a building emergency such as a power or water outage. The decision is made by 5:30 AM and announced through the Little Acorns Daily app, a text message to the primary contact, and a recorded message on the main phone line (614) 555-0138. Tuition is not reduced for weather closures.

title: Programs and Age Groups
body: We serve children from 6 weeks to 5 years old in four programs: Infants (6 weeks to 12 months, Robin Room), Toddlers (12 to 36 months, Sparrow Room), Preschool (3 to 4 years, Owl Room) and Pre-K (4 to 5 years, Hawk Room, kindergarten-readiness curriculum). Staff-to-child ratios are 1:4 for infants, 1:7 for toddlers, 1:10 for preschool and 1:12 for Pre-K. Maximum group sizes are 8 (infants), 14 (toddlers), 20 (preschool) and 24 (Pre-K). Children move up when they reach the age cutoff and have space available in the next room.

title: Weekly Tuition
body: Weekly tuition for full-time care (5 days): Infants $310, Toddlers $275, Preschool $235, Pre-K $225. Part-time care (3 days per week, Monday/Wednesday/Friday or Tuesday/Thursday plus one flexible day): Infants $215, Toddlers $190, Preschool $165, Pre-K $158. Tuition includes breakfast, lunch, an afternoon snack and curriculum materials covered by the annual supply fee. Diapers and wipes are not included; families supply their own. Tuition rates are reviewed each July and families receive 60 days' notice of any change.

title: Fees and Discounts
body: One-time registration fee: $75 per child. Annual supply fee: $100 per child, charged each September (or at enrollment). Waitlist fee: $50, applied toward the registration fee when a spot is offered. Sibling discount: 10% off the older child's tuition when two or more siblings are enrolled. Late payment fee: $15 if a payment is more than 3 days late. Returned payment fee: $25. Late pickup fee: $1.00 per minute after 6:05 PM. We do not currently offer other discounts.

title: Payment and Withdrawal
body: Tuition is paid weekly by automatic bank draft (ACH) every Friday for the following week. Tuition is charged for scheduled days whether or not your child attends (sick days, vacations and holidays are not credited). To withdraw your child, please give two weeks' written notice to the director; tuition is charged through the end of the notice period. Receipts for tax purposes are available each January from the front desk.

title: Illness and Exclusion Policy
body: Children must stay home or be picked up within one hour of being called if they have: a fever of 100.4°F or higher (they may return after 24 hours fever-free without fever-reducing medicine); vomiting or diarrhea (return after 24 hours symptom-free); a rash of unknown cause until a doctor says it's not contagious; pink eye with discharge (return 24 hours after starting treatment); strep throat (return after 12 hours of antibiotics and no fever); hand, foot and mouth disease (return when fever-free and blisters are scabbed or the doctor clears them); head lice (return after the first treatment and a nit check by staff). Please notify us the same day if your child is diagnosed with a contagious illness so we can inform other families without naming your child.

title: Medication and Allergies
body: Staff can give prescription or over-the-counter medication only with a signed Medication Authorization Form from a parent, and, for over-the-counter medicine, written dosage instructions from a doctor. Medication must be in its original container labeled with the child's name and dosage. Staff do not give medication on a parent's verbal request. Children with allergies need a written Allergy Action Plan from their doctor on file; staff are trained in epinephrine auto-injector use, and these plans are posted in the child's classroom. Medication is stored in a locked cabinet or the refrigerator.

title: Immunizations and Enrollment Documents
body: Required before the first day: completed enrollment packet, a current immunization record (or a medical or religious exemption form as allowed by Ohio law), a physical exam signed by a doctor within the last 12 months, emergency contact and authorized pickup list, a copy of the birth certificate, and signed tuition agreement. Updated immunization records are due whenever a new vaccine is given.

title: Meals and Snacks
body: Breakfast (8:00 AM), lunch (11:30 AM) and an afternoon snack (3:00 PM) are included in tuition. Meals are prepared in our kitchen by Chef Dana Whitfield, follow USDA child-care nutrition guidelines, and include a fruit or vegetable at every meal. Sample menu: Monday - oatmeal with fruit; turkey meatballs, brown rice and green beans. Tuesday - scrambled eggs and toast; cheese quesadilla with black beans and corn. Wednesday - whole-grain cereal and banana; baked chicken, sweet potato and peas. Thursday - yogurt and berries; whole-wheat pasta with vegetable marinara. Friday - pancakes with applesauce; fish sticks, carrots and roasted potatoes. Weekly menus are posted at the front desk and in the Little Acorns Daily app. Milk is whole for ages 1 to 2 and low-fat for age 2 and older.

title: Food Allergies, Outside Food and Infant Feeding
body: Little Acorns is a peanut-free and tree-nut-free facility. We accommodate other documented food allergies and dietary needs (including vegetarian and halal) with a signed Allergy Action Plan or dietary request; please tell the director at enrollment. Outside food is not permitted for meals; the exception is store-bought, individually packaged birthday treats that are nut-free, which must be approved by the teacher at least one day ahead. Infants: parents provide formula or breast milk in bottles labeled with the child's name and date, and we follow safe handling and storage guidelines. Solid foods are introduced only after the family tells us the child has tried them at home.

title: Tours
body: Tours are offered on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 10:00 AM and 4:30 PM and take about 30 minutes. You will meet the director, see the classroom for your child's age group and get an enrollment packet. To book, call the front desk at (614) 555-0138 or ask at the front desk during business hours; we cannot book tours through this app. Children are welcome to come along. Tours are not available during nap time or on holidays.

title: Enrollment Steps and Waitlist
body: Steps: (1) tour the center, (2) complete the enrollment packet and pay the $75 registration fee, (3) submit required documents, (4) schedule a short visit day before the start date. If a spot isn't available for your child's age group, you can join the waitlist with a $50 fee that is applied to registration when a spot opens. We contact waitlisted families in the order they joined, and then you have 3 business days to accept an offered spot. Infant spots have the longest waits, often 3 to 6 months.

title: Daily Schedule and Nap Time
body: A typical day: 6:30-8:00 arrival and free play; 8:00 breakfast; 8:45 circle time; 9:15 learning centers and art; 10:15 outdoor play (weather permitting); 11:30 lunch; 12:15-2:45 nap or quiet rest time; 3:00 snack; 3:30 outdoor play or music; 4:30-6:00 free play and pickup. Children who don't sleep rest quietly with books after 45 minutes. Infants follow their own sleep and feeding schedules. We provide cots and sheets; families bring a small blanket.

title: What to Bring
body: Every child needs: two complete changes of weather-appropriate clothes, a labeled water bottle, a small blanket and (optionally) a small stuffed animal for nap time, and sunscreen with a signed authorization if you want it applied. Infants and children in diapers need diapers and wipes; please label everything with your child's name. Pre-K children also need a backpack and indoor shoes. Please leave valuables at home.

title: Potty Training, Birthdays and Toys from Home
body: Potty training: we partner with families and begin when your child shows readiness; please send several extra changes of clothes. Birthdays: we celebrate in the classroom with a song and a nut-free treat (see Food Allergies policy). Toys from home: toys are discouraged because they get lost or cause conflict, except for a comfort item at nap time. Show-and-tell days are announced by the teacher.

title: Pickup, Drop-off and Safety
body: The building has a keypad-secured entrance; each family receives a personal door code. Only people on the authorized pickup list may collect a child, and staff check photo ID for anyone they don't know. Parents can update the list through the front desk or in writing; we cannot accept changes by phone alone. If an unlisted person arrives, we call the parent and do not release the child until we have confirmation. If staff believe a person is unfit to drive, we will offer to call another adult and, if necessary, the police. All staff pass background checks and a fingerprint check before working with children.

title: Emergency Procedures and Incident Reports
body: We practice fire drills monthly, severe-weather drills quarterly, and lockdown drills twice a year. In an evacuation, children go to the church parking lot across Willow Creek Drive and parents are notified by text. All staff are trained in pediatric CPR and first aid. For any injury, a written incident report is given to the parent at pickup, and parents are called right away for head injuries or anything needing medical care. Serious emergencies are handled by calling 911 first, then the family.

title: Staff, Qualifications and Licensing
body: Director Maria Delgado holds a bachelor's degree in Early Childhood Education and has led the center since 2016. Lead teachers have an associate's degree or Child Development Associate (CDA) credential; assistants have at least a high school diploma and ongoing training. All staff complete 15 hours of training each year, including CPR, first aid and safe sleep. Little Acorns is licensed by the Ohio Department of Children and Youth (License #CC-2016-04417) and inspection reports are available at the front desk.

title: Contact Information and Location
body: Little Acorns Learning Center, 4821 Willow Creek Drive, Maple Grove, OH 43017. Phone: (614) 555-0138. Email: hello@littleacorns.example. The front desk is staffed during open hours, Monday through Friday 6:30 AM to 6:00 PM. Director: Maria Delgado. There is a front parking lot with a short-term drop-off lane.

title: Communication with Parents
body: Teachers send daily updates (meals, naps, diapers, activities and photos) through the Little Acorns Daily app. Urgent messages are sent by text to the primary contact. Parent-teacher conferences are offered twice a year, in October and April, and you may request a meeting at any time. The center newsletter goes out on the first of every month. Please keep your contact information up to date with the front desk.
